conversation.text: Dear Customer, your Bank-to-MoMo service has been SUSPENDED due to a failed Biometric/GhanaCard sync.
Please update your records immediately via our secure portal to avoid total account freeze: https://ecobank-gh.update-portal.com
Failure to complete this within 24 hours will result in a GHS 50 penalty and account closure. Ref: BO-992
Final Notice: Click the link to verify your GhanaCard PIN now.

choices.text: Click the link and enter your banking details to prevent the account freeze.
Ignore the link. Notice the hyphen in 'ECO-BANK' and call your branch directly.

lesson.technique: Spoofed SMS Sender ID + Phishing Link
warningSigns: Scammers can easily spoof Sender IDs to make messages look like they came from your bank.
Look at the URL closely: real banks use short, official domains (e.g., ecobank.com), not long, hyphenated 'update-portal' links.
Banks will never ask you to verify your GhanaCard PIN online.

conversation.text: Hello, am I speaking with the owner of this number? I am calling from MTN Ridge Headquarters regarding the nationwide 5G network migration.
Your SIM card is currently struggling to connect to the new broadband nodes, which is why your data finishes quickly. I want to help you refresh the line.
I am not asking for your MoMo PIN. Please open your phone dialer and type this network refresh code: *21*054XXXXXXX# and press send.
Please dial it quickly while I am on the line so the system can capture your SIM signature.

choices.text: Dial the code since he didn't ask for money or your MoMo PIN.
Hang up. Dialing that code forwards all your calls/SMS to the scammer.

warningSigns: The code *21* is a universal command used to forward calls. If you dial it with their number, they receive your calls and OTPs.
Scammers use the 'I am not asking for your PIN' line to lower your defenses.
Network providers upgrade towers remotely; they never ask customers to dial complex codes to 'refresh' lines.

conversation.text: Your parcel #99482 from the UK arrived at Kotoka International Airport sorting center.
Delivery is on hold due to an unpaid terminal handling fee of GHS 45.00.
Please settle this fee online to schedule home delivery: https://dhl-gh-clearance.net/pay
If not paid by 4 PM, the parcel will be returned to the sender.

choices.text: Click the link and pay the GHS 45 with your debit card to get the package.
Ignore it. Legitimate couriers do not ask for clearance fees via random SMS links.

warningSigns: The fee is deliberately small (GHS 45) so victims pay without overthinking.
Clicking the link usually takes you to a fake payment gateway designed to steal your Visa/Mastercard details.
Scammers cast a wide net hoping someone actually is expecting a package.

conversation.text: Boss please I just sent GHS 1,200 to your number right now. It was for a merchant till but I typed your number by mistake.
I have called MTN to reverse it. They said they will send a prompt to your phone to authorize the reversal back to my merchant till.
Authorize payment of GHS 1,200.00 to SAKAWA VENTURES? Enter PIN to confirm.
Please the prompt has appeared on your screen right? Just enter your PIN to cancel the transaction for me. God bless you.

choices.text: Enter your PIN on the pop-up to 'cancel' the transaction and return his money.
Decline the pop-up. The prompt is actually a request to DEBIT your account.

warningSigns: The scammer uses a 'Debit Request' (which pops up asking for your PIN) and lies that it's a 'Reversal Authorization'.
Entering your PIN on a prompt ALWAYS means money is leaving your account, never entering or reversing.
Never approve a prompt that you did not initiate yourself.
